sections.hypothesis: Weeks after a coin's Wikipedia pageviews rose above their recent level return more than weeks after they didn't, by more than costs.
sections.rationale: Economic reason: attention brings new, mostly retail buyers over the following days, so a rise in attention comes before buying pressure. Outside evidence: Liu and Tsyvinski (Risks and Returns of Cryptocurrency, Review of Financial Studies 2021) find investor attention is one of the two strongest crypto return predictors: one standard deviation more Google searches came before a 1.84% higher Bitcoin return the next week. Wikipedia pageviews stand in for Google searches (no clean long daily Google history); Kristoufek (2013) used both for Bitcoin. Risk: attention rises with price, so it may only be weekly momentum, which failed out of sample here; the study reports that overlap. Luke chose this study (2026-11-14); nothing about attention and returns had been looked at.
sections.rules: kestrel signal-study attention BTCUSDT ETHUSDT --research <this note>: daily bars before 2025-11-01; at each Sunday close, the signal is on when the last 7 known days of pageviews (a day's count is known two days later, after it is published) exceed the average week of the 4 weeks before; outcome: log return from that close to the next Sunday's; weeks with a missing bar are skipped.
sections.falsification: PROCEED only if P(spread > 0) is at least 90% and the spread (mean week after on minus after off) is above 0.22%; otherwise KILL, and no strategy is built. If PROCEED but the on-weeks are mostly weeks after a rising week (the momentum overlap), the strategy note must say so and beat weekly momentum, not just holding. Run once.
sections.parameters: Sunday closes (UTC), the next 7 days, BTCUSDT and ETHUSDT 1d, pooled; 5,000 bootstrap resamples; no setting chosen after looking.
sections.costs: Hurdle 0.22%: one round trip of the taker fee and half-spread from kestrel.toml. A study, not a strategy run: one look, logged in the findings.
